name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
warningSignals: Refinery utilization sensitivity to crude-oil price volatility; Q3 2024 margin compression vs. Q2 amid WTI weakness
Geopolitical crude-supply disruption risk (Middle East, Russia sanctions); hedging costs rising
Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) compliance cost escalation; biodiesel/ethanol blending mandates pressure margins
Capital intensity of downstream transition (low-carbon fuels, hydrogen); CapEx guidance 2025–2027 elevated
opportunitySignals: Midstream integration via MPLX LP (MPC owns 69% as of 2024); fee-based cash flow de-risks commodity exposure
Advantaged refinery footprint (Gulf Coast, Midwest) positioned for heavy-sour crude processing; 3.1M bbl/day capacity
Renewable diesel / sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) capacity expansion; 2024 capex targeting 100K bbl/day by 2027
Potential M&A consolidation in refining sector; MPC's scale and balance sheet enable bolt-on acquisitions

enginesRun: Refinery operations optimization (crude-slate switching, yield management)
Renewable fuels capacity ramp (renewable diesel, SAF co-processing)
engineOutputs: Q3 2024 refining margin: $8.2/bbl (vs. $12.1/bbl Q2 2024); seasonal demand weakness
MPLX distributable cash flow: $1.8B annualized (2024 run rate)
Renewable diesel production: 35K bbl/day (2024); target 100K bbl/day by 2027

domainRelevance: Marathon Petroleum is the largest independent U.S. refiner by capacity (3.1M bbl/day across 16 refineries) and a critical node in the downstream petroleum supply chain, converting crude oil into transportation fuels, heating oil, and petrochemical feedstocks for industrial and consumer markets. The company's Gulf Coast and Midwest refinery footprint processes heavy-sour crude, capturing value from price differentials and serving regional demand centers. Via 69%-owned MPLX LP, MPC operates 15,000+ miles of crude and product pipelines, providing fee-based midstream revenue that stabilizes earnings against commodity-price swings.
portalRelevance: Marathon Petroleum is a tier-1 anchor in the energy domain and a critical counterparty for crude-oil producers, logistics providers, and fuel distributors. Its refining margins, capacity utilization, and crude-slate decisions directly signal downstream fuel-cost inflation/deflation for transportation and heating sectors. The company's renewable-fuels transition and MPLX fee-based cash flow are key indicators of energy-sector structural change and capital-allocation discipline; MPC's dividend and buyback policy reflect management's confidence in long-cycle refining economics.

notes.cohortStatus: Anchor refiner; peer group includes Valero Energy, Phillips 66, HollyFrontier
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW; strong balance sheet, positive free cash flow, dividend-backed equity

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly crude-oil price (WTI/Brent) and refining-margin prints (crack spreads: 3-2-1, 5-3-2)
Monthly refinery utilization rates and crude-throughput volumes (disclosed in earnings)
Quarterly MPLX fee-based revenue and distributable cash flow; pipeline utilization metrics
8-K filings for M&A activity, asset sales, or major operational incidents (unplanned downtime)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Refining margin trajectory (3-month rolling average vs. 5-year median); phase classification (contraction vs. expansion)
Free cash flow generation and debt/EBITDA ratio; cash-deployment priorities (dividend, buyback, debt reduction)
Renewable-fuels capacity ramp progress; SAF co-processing utilization rates
MPLX distribution growth and MPC's equity-method earnings contribution to consolidated net income

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Margin compression pattern-match: identify if driven by crude-supply disruption, demand shock, or capacity glut
Geopolitical crude-supply risk assessment; correlation with sanctions regimes and OPEC+ production decisions
Renewable-fuels transition risk: RFS compliance cost vs. SAF premium realization; competitive positioning vs. Valero/Phillips 66
Midstream fee-revenue stability check: MPLX volume growth decoupled from commodity-price volatility

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: EPA Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) compliance strategy; biodiesel/ethanol blending mandate cost hedging
SEC disclosure of climate-risk scenario analysis (Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures compliance)
DOT pipeline-safety compliance and PHMSA incident reporting; crude-by-rail logistics regulation
FTC antitrust monitoring post-Andeavor acquisition (2019); market-concentration thresholds in key regions

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Crude-slate optimization: shift to heavy-sour crude when WTI-Brent spread widens; light-sweet when spread narrows
Capital allocation: prioritize MPLX distribution growth and renewable-fuels capex; maintain dividend at 4–5% yield
Hedging: crude-oil and product-margin futures/swaps to lock in 60–70% of expected refining spread
M&A screening: evaluate bolt-on refinery acquisitions or renewable-fuels assets if valuation <6x EBITDA

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings release: compare actual refining margin vs. guidance; assess crude-throughput variance
Monthly refinery-utilization data (via industry reports); track unplanned downtime impact on cash flow
MPLX quarterly distribution announcement; monitor fee-revenue growth vs. volume growth decoupling
Stock-price reaction to earnings and guidance; implied refining-margin expectations from options market

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Recalibrate crude-slate sensitivity model based on realized WTI-Brent spread volatility and MPC's actual switching costs
Update MPLX fee-revenue growth assumptions if volume growth decelerates or tariff structure changes
Reassess renewable-fuels transition timeline if SAF premium realization lags or RFS compliance costs spike
Adjust peer-group beta and correlation assumptions if MPC's margin profile diverges from Valero/Phillips 66 due to refinery-mix differences

functionalNetwork.model: Marathon Petroleum operates as a distributed refining and logistics network, functioning as a neural hub that converts crude-oil signals (price, supply disruption, geopolitical risk) into downstream fuel-supply decisions. The company's 16 refineries act as parallel processing nodes, each optimizing crude-slate and yield based on local demand and feedstock costs. MPLX LP serves as a fee-based stabilizer, decoupling earnings from commodity volatility. Upstream crude suppliers, logistics partners, and fuel customers form the sensory and motor periphery; regulators and capital providers constrain the decision space; competitors and market signals provide competitive context.

suppliers.name: Saudi Aramco
suppliers.relationshipNote: Saudi Aramco is a primary crude-oil supplier to MPC's Gulf Coast refineries, with long-term supply agreements covering ~400K bbl/day of Arab Light and Arab Heavy crude. MPC's crude-slate flexibility allows switching between Saudi, Russian (pre-sanctions), and West African grades to optimize refining margins. 2024 supply disruptions (Houthi Red Sea attacks) elevated crude-transport costs; MPC hedged via longer-haul sourcing from Brazil and Guyana.

suppliers.name: Equinor ASA
suppliers.relationshipNote: Equinor supplies North Sea Brent crude to MPC's East Coast and Midwest refineries via long-term contracts (~200K bbl/day). 2022 energy crisis and Norwegian production volatility increased MPC's reliance on alternative suppliers (Guyana, Brazil). Equinor's renewable-energy portfolio (offshore wind) creates potential future partnership for MPC's low-carbon fuels strategy.

suppliers.name: Chevron Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Chevron supplies heavy-sour crude from Kern County (California) and international operations to MPC's West Coast and Gulf Coast refineries (~150K bbl/day). MPC's 2019 Andeavor acquisition included Chevron-supplied feedstock contracts. Chevron's renewable-fuels joint ventures (e.g., Chevron Renewable Energy Group) create potential co-processing opportunities for MPC's SAF expansion.

suppliers.name: Valero Energy Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Valero is MPC's primary refining competitor (3.3M bbl/day capacity vs. MPC's 3.1M bbl/day) and competes for crude-oil supply contracts in the Gulf Coast and Midwest. Both companies source heavy-sour crude from OPEC and non-OPEC suppliers; crude-price differentials and refining-margin spreads drive competitive positioning. 2024 refining margins compressed for both; Valero's renewable-diesel capacity (100K bbl/day) slightly exceeds MPC's, creating competitive pressure on SAF economics.

suppliers.name: Enbridge Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Enbridge operates the Mainline crude-oil pipeline system (2.8M bbl/day capacity) that supplies MPC's Midwest refineries with Canadian heavy crude and U.S. domestic production. MPC's crude-slate decisions depend on Enbridge tariff structures and pipeline utilization; 2023 Mainline debottlenecking project increased MPC's access to Canadian bitumen. Enbridge's renewable-fuels logistics initiatives align with MPC's low-carbon transition strategy.

suppliers.name: Tronox Holdings plc
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tronox supplies titanium dioxide and specialty chemicals used in MPC's petrochemical co-product streams (lubricants, additives). MPC's refinery yield optimization includes specialty-chemical extraction; Tronox's supply-chain resilience (2022 supply-chain disruptions) affects MPC's downstream margin realization.

suppliers.name: Lyondell Basell Industries N.V.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Lyondell Basell is a major offtaker of MPC's petrochemical co-products (propylene, butadiene, benzene) from Gulf Coast refineries. MPC's refinery-yield optimization targets high-value chemical streams; Lyondell's demand signals and contract pricing directly impact MPC's margin realization. 2024 chemical-industry weakness (polyethylene oversupply) pressured co-product prices; MPC adjusted crude-slate to maximize fuel yield.

suppliers.name: Cargill Incorporated
suppliers.relationshipNote: Cargill supplies vegetable oils (soybean, canola) and animal fats to MPC's renewable-diesel production units. MPC's renewable-diesel capacity (35K bbl/day, 2024) depends on feedstock availability and pricing; Cargill's agricultural commodity exposure creates feedstock-cost volatility. 2024 soybean-oil prices elevated renewable-diesel margins; MPC's SAF expansion targets waste-based feedstocks (used cooking oil) to reduce Cargill dependency.

suppliers.name: Nouryon (Akzo Nobel subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Nouryon supplies caustic soda and chlorine used in MPC's refinery operations (water treatment, corrosion control). Nouryon's hydrogen production (via chlor-alkali process) is relevant to MPC's future hydrogen-for-refining strategy.

suppliers.name: Magellan Midstream Partners L.P.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Magellan operates 9,600 miles of refined-product pipelines and 50+ terminals; MPC ships ~1.5M bbl/day of gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel via Magellan's network to regional distribution centers. Magellan's tariff structure and capacity utilization directly impact MPC's product-delivery costs and margin realization. 2024 Magellan capex expansion (renewable-fuels logistics) supports MPC's SAF distribution strategy.

logisticsPartners.name: MPLX LP
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: MPLX LP is 69%-owned by MPC and operates 15,000+ miles of crude and product pipelines, 50+ terminals, and logistics assets. MPLX generated $1.8B annualized distributable cash flow (2024), providing MPC with fee-based revenue decoupled from commodity prices. MPC's 2024 capex guidance ($2.1B) includes MPLX renewable-fuels logistics expansion; MPLX's fee-growth trajectory is critical to MPC's earnings stability.

logisticsPartners.name: Kinder Morgan Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Kinder Morgan operates crude-oil and refined-product pipelines that complement MPLX's network, serving MPC's Gulf Coast and Midwest refineries. KMI's Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America (NGPL) transports natural gas used in MPC's refinery operations. 2024 KMI capex includes renewable-fuels logistics; MPC and KMI collaborate on SAF distribution infrastructure.

logisticsPartners.name: Schneider National Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Schneider National operates truck fleets and logistics networks that distribute MPC's refined products (gasoline, diesel) to retail fuel stations and commercial customers. Schneider's 2024 fleet electrification initiatives align with MPC's renewable-fuels strategy.

logisticsPartners.name: Suncor Energy Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Suncor supplies Canadian oil-sands crude to MPC's Midwest refineries via Enbridge and other pipeline systems (~300K bbl/day). Suncor's production volatility (maintenance, weather) affects MPC's crude-slate planning. 2024 Suncor capex includes renewable-fuels co-processing; potential future partnership for MPC's SAF expansion.

customers.name: Pilot Flying J
customers.relationshipNote: Pilot Flying J operates 750+ travel centers across North America; MPC supplies diesel and gasoline to Pilot's retail network (~200K bbl/day). Pilot's fuel-margin pressure (2024 competitive pricing) affects MPC's downstream revenue. Pilot's EV-charging infrastructure expansion creates future alternative-fuel opportunity for MPC.

customers.name: United Airlines Holdings Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: United Airlines is a major offtaker of MPC's jet fuel (Jet A-1) from Gulf Coast refineries (~50K bbl/day equivalent). United's 2024 sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) mandate (10% blending by 2030) creates demand signal for MPC's SAF expansion. MPC's renewable-diesel co-processing units can produce SAF; United's long-term SAF contracts support MPC's capex ROI.

customers.name: Chevron Products Company
customers.relationshipNote: Chevron Products distributes MPC's refined products (gasoline, diesel) under supply agreements covering ~400K bbl/day. Chevron's retail network (Chevron, Texaco brands) is a key outlet for MPC's fuel production. 2024 Chevron renewable-fuels initiatives (e.g., Chevron Renewable Energy Group) create co-processing opportunities for MPC's SAF.

competitors.name: Valero Energy Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Valero is the largest independent U.S. refiner (3.3M bbl/day capacity vs. MPC's 3.1M bbl/day). Both companies compete for crude-oil supply, refining margins, and fuel-distribution market share. 2024 refining margins compressed for both; Valero's renewable-diesel capacity (100K bbl/day) slightly exceeds MPC's. Valero's dividend yield (3.8%) and buyback program mirror MPC's capital-allocation strategy.

competitors.name: Phillips 66
competitors.relationshipNote: Phillips 66 operates 2.0M bbl/day of refining capacity and competes with MPC in the Gulf Coast and Midwest. PSX's downstream segment (fuel distribution, logistics) is smaller than MPC's MPLX, creating competitive advantage for MPC. 2024 PSX capex includes renewable-fuels expansion; PSX's midstream partnership (Targa Resources) provides fee-based revenue similar to MPC's MPLX model.

competitors.name: HollyFrontier Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: HollyFrontier operates 1.0M bbl/day of refining capacity (smaller than MPC) and competes in the Midwest and Southwest. HollyFrontier's 2023 merger with HF Sinclair created a 1.3M bbl/day combined entity; HF Sinclair is now a separate competitor. MPC's scale advantage (3.1M bbl/day) provides better crude-sourcing leverage and margin stability.

competitors.name: Delek US Holdings Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Delek operates 0.6M bbl/day of refining capacity (smaller independent refiner). Delek competes with MPC in the Midwest and Gulf Coast but lacks MPC's scale and midstream integration. 2024 Delek capex focused on maintenance; MPC's renewable-fuels expansion creates competitive advantage.

competitors.name: Saudi Aramco
competitors.relationshipNote: Saudi Aramco is a vertically integrated competitor (upstream crude production, downstream refining, retail). Aramco's 2024 refining capacity expansion (Yanbu refinery) increases global refining supply, pressuring MPC's margins. Aramco's renewable-fuels initiatives (hydrogen, SAF) create competitive pressure on MPC's low-carbon transition strategy.

competitors.name: Valero Energy Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Valero operates competing retail fuel networks and competes with MPC for crude-oil supply and fuel-distribution market share. Both companies' refining margins and product pricing are correlated; 2024 margin compression affected both equally. Valero's renewable-diesel capacity (100K bbl/day) exceeds MPC's, creating competitive pressure on SAF economics and renewable-fuels market share.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees MPC's 10-K/10-Q filings, proxy statements (DEF14A), and 8-K event disclosures. MPC's 2024 climate-risk disclosure (Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures) is subject to SEC scrutiny. SEC's proposed climate-disclosure rules (effective 2025) will require MPC to disclose Scope 1/2/3 GHG emissions and climate-scenario analysis.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates MPC's refinery air and water emissions under the Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act. MPC's 16 refineries hold EPA air permits and NPDES water permits; 2024 EPA enforcement actions on refineries (e.g., Tesoro Anacortes) signal tighter compliance expectations. EPA's Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) mandates 15B gallons of renewable fuels annually; MPC's renewable-diesel production (35K bbl/day) contributes to RFS compliance.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Transportation / Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: PHMSA regulates MPC's crude-oil and refined-product pipelines (via MPLX) under 49 CFR Part 195. MPC's 15,000+ miles of pipelines require PHMSA permits and incident reporting. 2024 PHMSA focus on pipeline integrity management and cybersecurity creates compliance cost for MPC.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors MPC's market concentration and competitive practices. MPC's 2019 Andeavor acquisition (creating MPC's current 3.1M bbl/day capacity) was approved with divestitures. FTC's 2024 focus on energy-sector consolidation creates scrutiny for any future M&A by MPC.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Energy
regulators.relationshipNote: DOE monitors U.S. refining capacity and fuel supply security. MPC's 3.1M bbl/day capacity represents ~9% of U.S. refining; DOE considers MPC critical to national energy security. DOE's 2024 renewable-fuels grants and hydrogen-hub funding create opportunities for MPC's low-carbon transition capex.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is MPC's independent auditor (Big Four) and provides audit services for MPC's consolidated financial statements and internal controls (SOX 404 compliance). Deloitte's 2024 audit opinion covers MPC's refining operations, MPLX equity-method accounting, and renewable-fuels asset valuation. Deloitte's audit fees (~$8M annually) are disclosed in MPC's proxy statement.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is a lead arranger of MPC's $3.5B revolving credit facility (2024 renewal) and provides investment-banking services for MPC's debt issuances and M&A. JPMorgan's energy-sector research team provides market intelligence on crude-oil prices and refining margins. JPMorgan's 2024 energy-sector outlook influences MPC's capital-allocation decisions.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is a co-arranger of MPC's credit facility and provides debt-capital markets services. BofA's energy-sector equity research covers MPC; BofA's 2024 refining-margin forecasts influence MPC's guidance and capital-allocation strategy. BofA's institutional clients (pension funds, asset managers) are major holders of MPC equity and debt.

capitalProviders.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Berkshire Hathaway owns ~5.2% of MPC (as of 2024), making it a major equity holder. Berkshire's long-term energy-sector thesis (dividend-yielding, cash-generative assets) aligns with MPC's capital-allocation strategy. Berkshire's CEO Warren Buffett's public skepticism of energy-sector transition creates governance tension with MPC's renewable-fuels capex.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is a major institutional holder of MPC equity (~8% of shares outstanding, 2024). Vanguard's ESG-focused funds have reduced MPC exposure; Vanguard's engagement with MPC on climate-risk disclosure influences MPC's sustainability reporting. Vanguard's voting power on MPC's board elections creates governance leverage.

executiveTeam.name: Andrey Tarasov
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Andrey Tarasov is President and Chief Executive Officer of Marathon Petroleum (appointed 2023). Tarasov leads MPC's strategic direction, including renewable-fuels capex expansion and MPLX fee-revenue growth. Tarasov's 2024 guidance emphasized margin recovery and disciplined capital allocation; his background in downstream operations (prior roles at Gazprom, Surgutneftegaz) influences MPC's crude-slate strategy.

executiveTeam.name: Maryann T. Mannen
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Maryann T. Mannen is Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Marathon Petroleum. Mannen oversees MPC's financial planning, capital allocation, and investor relations. Mannen's 2024 guidance on free cash flow ($2.8B–$3.2B) and debt-reduction targets reflects disciplined financial management. Mannen's background in energy-sector finance influences MPC's hedging and risk-management strategy.

executiveTeam.name: Michael J. Stice
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Michael J. Stice is Executive Vice President of Refining Operations at Marathon Petroleum. Stice oversees MPC's 16 refineries and crude-slate optimization. Stice's operational expertise in heavy-sour crude processing and yield optimization is critical to MPC's margin realization. Stice's 2024 focus on renewable-fuels co-processing integration influences MPC's SAF expansion timeline.

executiveTeam.name: Kristina A. Kazarian
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Kristina A. Kazarian is Executive Vice President, General Counsel, and Secretary of Marathon Petroleum. Kazarian oversees MPC's legal, compliance, and regulatory affairs. Kazarian's 2024 focus includes climate-risk disclosure compliance (SEC rules), EPA environmental-permit management, and antitrust monitoring. Kazarian's background in energy-sector law influences MPC's regulatory strategy.

marketSignals.name: WTI Crude Oil Spot Price (NYMEX)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: WTI crude-oil spot price is the primary input signal for MPC's refining-margin calculation. MPC's crude-slate decisions and hedging strategy depend on WTI-Brent spread dynamics. 2024 WTI volatility (range: $65–$85/bbl) created margin compression; MPC's hedging program locked in 60–70% of expected spreads to stabilize earnings.

marketSignals.name: Refining Margin Index (3-2-1 Crack Spread)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: The 3-2-1 crack spread (3 barrels crude → 2 barrels gasoline + 1 barrel diesel) is MPC's primary margin indicator. 2024 Q3 crack spread averaged $8.2/bbl (vs. $12.1/bbl Q2), signaling margin compression. MPC's quarterly guidance adjusts for crack-spread expectations; market consensus on 2025 spreads ($9–$11/bbl) influences MPC's capital-allocation decisions.

marketSignals.name: U.S. Refinery Utilization Rate
marketSignals.relationshipNote: U.S. refinery utilization rate (published by EIA) is a demand signal for MPC's production. 2024 utilization averaged 92% (vs. 94% in 2023), indicating demand softness. MPC's utilization guidance (92–94% for 2025) reflects expected seasonal demand patterns and competitive capacity additions.
